pluss::note::print¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

std::string  pluss::note::print(const Note& n)
std::string  pluss::note::print(const Note& n, const NotePrintOptions& opt)
std::ostream& pluss::note::print(std::ostream& os, const Note& n,
                                 const NotePrintOptions& opt = {})

Render A Note For Inspection¶

print() produces the human-readable representation of a Note — the form this reference uses in every ### Output block. It mirrors pluss::series::print and pluss::timeline::print.

It is a rendering function, not a constructor: it does not build or modify a Note. It lives in the factory namespace because it is the natural companion to the builders — the thing you reach for immediately after making one.

The first two overloads return a std::string and write nothing themselves; you print or log the result. The third overload writes straight to os and returns the stream for chaining. Streaming a Note directly (std::cout << n) also works and is equivalent to print(std::cout, n) with default options.

print() has no side effects and is deterministic. An undefined Note renders as Note(undefined).

The Default Layout¶

With default options the output is a header line followed by the values:

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["one", "two", "three"]

  • Header — Note( then shape, dim, numel, and encoding (utf8 or bytes), then ).

  • Values — laid out by rank:

    • rank 0 (scalar): the single cell alone, e.g. "Final Exam Review".

    • rank 1: a one-line bracketed list, ["a", "b", "c"].

    • rank 2 and 3: an indented block, one nested list per row.

Each text cell is escaped and wrapped in quotes: "..." for UTF-8 mode, b"..." for bytes mode. Control bytes and DEL become \xNN (with \n, \t, … for the named ones) in both modes; in bytes mode every byte >= 0x80 is escaped too, so the escaped view is always plain ASCII. In bytes mode with bytes_mode = Hex, cells render as hex[de ad be ef] instead.

NotePrintOptions Fields¶

All fields have defaults; construct the struct and set only what you need.

Layout¶

Field

Type

Default

Effect

edge_items

std::int64_t

2

When the output is summarised, how many leading and trailing cells to show per axis before the ... marker.

max_elements

std::int64_t

256

Summarise (insert ...) when numel exceeds this and edge_items > 0. Set to 0 to never summarise.

max_cell_chars

std::int64_t

96

Cap on the inner content of each cell. Longer content is cut and ends with ... (a plain cut when the budget is ≤ 3). Quotes and hex[]/b"" delimiters are added after clipping, so a clipped cell is never left unbalanced. Set to 0 to never clip.

Header¶

Field

Type

Default

Effect

metadata_mode

NotePrintMetadataMode

Full

Full — emit the header, honouring the four show_* toggles below. Compact — a terse one-liner, shape and encoding only. None — no header line at all.

content_mode

NotePrintContentMode

Both

Both — header and values. HeaderOnly — the header line only. ValuesOnly — the values only.

show_shape

bool

true

Include shape=[...] in a Full header.

show_dim

bool

true

Include dim=N in a Full header.

show_numel

bool

true

Include numel=N in a Full header.

show_encoding

bool

true

Include `encoding=utf8

Cell text¶

Field

Type

Default

Effect

bytes_mode

NotePrintBytesMode

Escaped

Escaped — b"..." with C-style escapes. Hex — hex[de ad]. Affects bytes-mode Notes only.

quote_strings

bool

true

Wrap each cell in quotes. false prints the bare cell text.

escape_controls

bool

true

Render control and DEL bytes as \xNN (plus \n, \t, …); in bytes mode this also escapes every byte >= 0x80. false emits all of them literally.

Related enums¶

enum class NotePrintMetadataMode { Full, Compact, None };
enum class NotePrintContentMode  { Both, HeaderOnly, ValuesOnly };
enum class NotePrintBytesMode    { Escaped, Hex };

All three are available unqualified as pluss::NotePrintMetadataMode, pluss::NotePrintContentMode, and pluss::NotePrintBytesMode.

Example 1: Default Rendering Of A Column¶

const auto col = pluss::note::make({"one", "two", "three"});  // reused below
std::cout << pluss::note::print(col) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["one", "two", "three"]

Example 2: A Scalar¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::make("Final Exam Review")) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"Final Exam Review"

Example 3: A Two-Dimensional Block¶

const pluss::Note block = pluss::note::make({{"r0c0", "r0c1"}, {"r1c0", "r1c1"}});
std::cout << block << "\n";  // operator<< == print() with default options

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["r0c0", "r0c1"], 
  ["r1c0", "r1c1"]
]

Example 4: Header Only¶

pluss::NotePrintOptions opt;
opt.content_mode = pluss::NotePrintContentMode::HeaderOnly;
std::cout << pluss::note::print(col, opt) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)

Just the metadata — useful for logging shape without dumping content.

Example 5: Values Only¶

pluss::NotePrintOptions opt;
opt.content_mode = pluss::NotePrintContentMode::ValuesOnly;
std::cout << pluss::note::print(col, opt) << "\n";

Output¶

["one", "two", "three"]

Example 6: No Header At All¶

pluss::NotePrintOptions opt;
opt.metadata_mode = pluss::NotePrintMetadataMode::None;
std::cout << pluss::note::print(col, opt) << "\n";

Output¶

["one", "two", "three"]

metadata_mode = None with the default content_mode = Both prints the values with no leading blank line.

Example 7: Compact Header¶

pluss::NotePrintOptions opt;
opt.metadata_mode = pluss::NotePrintMetadataMode::Compact;
std::cout << pluss::note::print(col, opt) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], encoding=utf8)
["one", "two", "three"]

dim and numel are dropped — both follow from shape.

Example 8: Summarising A Long Column¶

pluss::NotePrintOptions opt;
opt.edge_items = 1;
opt.max_elements = 3;
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"}), opt) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
["a", ..., "f"]

numel (6) exceeds max_elements (3), so only edge_items (1) cell at each end is shown.

Example 9: Unquoted Cells¶

pluss::NotePrintOptions opt;
opt.quote_strings = false;
std::cout << pluss::note::print(col, opt) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
[one, two, three]

Example 10: Clipping Wide Cells¶

pluss::NotePrintOptions opt;
opt.max_cell_chars = 12;
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"short", "a-much-longer-cell-value"}), opt) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["short", "a-much-..."]

"short" fits; the long cell is cut to the budget and closed with ... — and the closing quote is still there.

Example 11: Writing Straight To A Stream¶

const auto col = pluss::note::make({"one", "two", "three"});
pluss::note::print(std::cout, col) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["one", "two", "three"]

The three-argument overload writes to the stream and returns it, so << can continue the line. std::cout << col alone does the same with default options.

See Also¶

  • pluss::note::make / pluss::note::bytes: the constructors whose results these examples render.

  • pluss::note::format: build a string; print shows a Note.
